summary: The study describes the use of W(CO)6 and H2O2 in an ALD-like process to grow WOx films on TiO2 nanoparticles. The process involves both ALD-like and chemical vapor deposition (CVD) growth modes, with the films inhibiting the anatase-to-rutile phase transformation in TiO2 upon annealing. The films were observed to be amorphous and conformal.
evidence: W(CO)6 and H2O2 were used in an atomic layer deposition (ALD)-like process to grow thin WOx films onto TiO2 powders in a fluidized bed reactor. The resulting WOx films were a result of both ALD-like and chemical vapor deposition-based growth modes. The films were observed to inhibit the anatase-to-rutile phase transformation in the Ti TiO2 powders upon high temperature annealing.
